1.why: The system enforces server-side authorization on MFA endpoints by deriving the account solely from the session (required() function).

2.why: The same verification code (IDENTITY_CODE) is hardcoded and would work for any user in TEST_MODE.

3.why: Previous sessions are not invalidated when MFA is enabled; only a new session is created (sessions.delete(old.id) in signin, but no cleanup in confirm).

4.why: OTP shared secret is stored encrypted (encryptedSecret in Mfa type) and backup codes are stored as salted PBKDF2 verifiers.

5.why: Secrets and codes are generated using crypto.getRandomValues (bytes() function).

6.why: Secrets, OTPs, and session tokens are not stored in browser storage or non-HttpOnly cookies (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies are used).

7.why: Server-side input validation is performed (e.g., email/phone format checks in signin, code/otp regex in identity/confirm).

8.why: Contextual output encoding is handled by the browser (no direct DOM injection; JSON responses are used).

9.why: Redirects are restricted to '/' (hardcoded in signin) and no open redirects are present.

10.why: Secure headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options) are set in the headers() function.

11.why: Session cookies are set with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict attributes (cookie() function).

12.why: OTP seeds, backup codes, and session tokens are not exposed in logs, URLs, or error output (only test values in TEST_MODE).

13.why: Verification codes (TOTP) are single-use and time-bound (30-second period in totp() function).

14.why: Rate-limiting is implemented (addFail() tracks failures and locks accounts after MAX attempts).

15.why: Session identifier is rotated on authentication (new session created in signin/identity), but idle/absolute timeouts are enforced (IDLE/ABS constants). However, logout invalidates only the current session (not all sessions for the user).
